issues.body:
## Outcome
Build an original premium antique 3D globe in the oracle's study. Users approach the same globe, browse region → country, then choose a city from that country's existing HTML search/list. Camera exploration stops at country framing; city selection does not move or zoom the globe. Existing manual latitude/longitude and IANA timezone entry remains available before proceeding to the crystal chart.

## Confirmed product direction
- Create our own meshes, textures and materials. The [CGTrader vintage globe](https://www.cgtrader.com/3d-models/science/other/vintage-globe-50e9e62e-547f-42a1-aa50-09b2ae7a3028) is a visual reference only; do not purchase, extract or reuse its assets.
- Raised terrain must be actual surface displacement, complemented by normal/bump detail. A plain smooth sphere is insufficient.
- Aged brass meridian ring, calibrated axis, crafted dark walnut stand, parchment cartography and restrained gold details; visual quality must hold at close zoom.
- Continuous camera and globe motion across room, region and country framing. Keep the same object/world anchor.
- Region categories include Europe, Asia, Middle East, Africa, North America, South America and Oceania. These are browsing regions, not a claim that Middle East is a continent. Provide All countries and explicit cross-region policy.

## Existing baseline
Main inspected at 92d78615 (2026-10-11). PR #61 is merged: GeoNames atlas provides 34,159 cities across 244 countries/territories, country-sharded lazy local search, manual coordinates/IANA timezone, local Rust/WASM calculation and natal reports. Reuse it.
Relevant boundaries: apps/web/src/features/astrology/BirthForm.tsx, packages/scenes/src/study.ts, packages/contracts/src/astrology-view.ts, content/astrology/atlas/README.md, docs/contracts/natal-scene.md.
Existing AstrologyView excludes location; add a separate minimal birthplace presentation contract instead of passing a BirthInput or chart record into rendering.

## Architecture constraints
Keep Next.js static export to S3, root Zustand state, one persistent renderer, separate feature engines, explicit save/delete and current chart compatibility. Scenes own presentation/picking/resources; application owns place selection and atlas lookup; Rust retains historical time conversion and chart calculations. Display geographic coordinates only through the dedicated view contract, never full birth records.
No birth data, searches or coordinates in URLs, logs, analytics or external requests. Static public data assets can load by version/country. No paid geocoder, nearest-city timezone guess or longitude-to-timezone formula.

## Completion
- Original reproducible globe assets with source/license/provenance records.
- Terrain, materials, geographic picking and camera transitions agree at representative locations.
- Globe and accessible HTML controls update one selection state; direct coordinate entry requires explicit IANA zone confirmation.
- Region/country camera transitions, city-list selection, backtracking, reduced motion, touch, failure recovery and route cancellation work.
- Existing natal and tarot behavior and saved results remain compatible.
- Measured download/GPU/frame costs and visual evidence; do not claim physical-device performance from emulation.
- All child issues complete with inspectable evidence.

## Delivery sequence
Contracts → geographic pipeline and original model → terrain/materials → room integration → navigation and chooser → resource optimization → integrated qualification.

## Child issues
- [ ] #64 — Define birthplace globe contracts, region taxonomy and navigation state
- [ ] #65 — Build reproducible geographic, elevation and region datasets for the globe
- [ ] #66 — Create original antique globe meshes, brass mount and walnut stand
- [ ] #67 — Implement raised terrain, antique cartography and premium material shading
- [ ] #68 — Integrate the original globe into the study and astrology scene lifecycle
- [ ] #69 — Implement continuous region → country globe camera navigation
- [ ] #70 — Connect globe and accessible birthplace chooser to the existing city atlas
- [ ] #71 — Optimize globe LOD, progressive loading and GPU resource budgets
- [ ] #72 — Qualify the complete antique globe birthplace experience and document evidence

## Dependency sequence
1. #64 establishes contracts.
2. #65 geographic/elevation data and #66 original mesh can proceed independently after #64.
3. #67 joins model, data and material work.
4. #68 integrates the globe into the study.
5. #69 adds continuous navigation; #70 connects and confirms birthplace selection.
6. #71 measures and optimizes the integrated experience.
7. #72 qualifies the complete delivery and regressions.

Each child links this epic and lists its prerequisites. The checklist records the hierarchy; native GitHub sub-issue relationships were not set because the available connector does not expose that operation.

## Scope boundary
The globe rotates/zooms only through region and country selection, with a bounded maximum country zoom. Cities are selected from the chosen country's existing HTML search/list while the camera stays fixed. Keep original premium meshes, real raised terrain and antique materials. City zoom, city terrain/label streaming, city pins and direct surface-coordinate picking are outside this delivery; retain the existing manual coordinate/timezone form.

issues.body:
## Outcome
Make the visible candle and desk lamp the believable sources of warm light in the oracle's study. Preserve the approved illustrated/pixel-art direction while making table camera movement reveal a genuinely three-dimensional lamp.

## Confirmed design
- Keep the candle body as authored sprite artwork. Separate its flame into an animated sprite/shader layer, with a PointLight anchored at the wick/flame.
- Coordinate flame sway/shape/glow with subtle continuous light flicker. Avoid independent random values per frame, rhythmic pulsing or aggressive scene-wide flashing.
- Build an original lamp Mesh using the supplied Aged bronze desk lamp(1).png as the form/style reference: flared fabric shade, curved aged-bronze stem, layered round base. Model the inside of the shade and retain pixel/painted texture character.
- Use emissive material for visible lamp glow and actual lights for illumination. Start with a downward SpotLight for the desk and bounded non-shadow fill if justified for the shade.
- Attach source lights to each prop's local anchors, never to the camera.
- Default to lamp as the main shadow-casting warm source and candle as a shadowless secondary source, with measured capability-based fallback.
- Existing unlit backgrounds/portraits/card artwork must stay visually coherent; preserve artwork color/readability rather than blindly converting every material to PBR.

## Baseline and references
Reviewed main at 92d78615. packages/scenes/src/tarot.ts already uses an ambient hemisphere, warm shadow-casting directional light, rim light, deskGlow/windowGlow/shoulderGlow PointLights. These are not authored candle/lamp assemblies. packages/scenes/src/study.ts places lamp/candle image layers; composition.ts uses unlit image materials.
User supplied candle.webp and Aged bronze desk lamp(1).png. Resolve and retain the supplied source files with hashes/provenance during implementation; do not assume issue viewers have access to temporary attachment paths.
Related globe epic #63; integration #68 and materials #67. Lighting work can proceed independently using representative test meshes; globe-specific visual qualification follows the actual globe implementation.

## Boundaries
Preserve one renderer, Next.js S3 static export, root Zustand, current tarot choreography/cameras/cards and astrology chart semantics. Scene-local animation and prop/light ownership remain presentation code; no Rust/WASM changes are expected. Keep shared asset leases, cancellation, cleanup and reduced-motion behavior.
No need for a full 3D room rebuild, candle-body Mesh, volumetric lighting, dynamic GI, or multiple shadow-casting point lights.

## Acceptance
- Candle flame and local illumination visibly agree without distracting flicker.
- Original Mesh lamp holds its silhouette and fabric/bronze character from conversation, oblique table and close camera views.
- Table, hands and available globe meshes respond to prop-anchored lights; lamp shade/blockers prevent obvious upward/backward light leakage.
- Background illustrations and cards remain readable with consistent warm/cool art direction.
- Room/astrology/tarot paths work with direct entry, reduced motion, interrupted preparation and repeated route changes.
- Record visual evidence and measured shadow/resource cost; do not infer physical-device qualification from emulation.
- Complete child acceptance criteria and existing meaningful regression gates.

## Child issues
- [ ] #74 — Define shared candle/lamp anchors and study lighting ownership
- [ ] #75 — Separate and animate the candle flame with synchronized local PointLight
- [ ] #76 — Author an original 3D bronze desk lamp matching the supplied artwork
- [ ] #77 — Implement lamp downlight, shade glow and bounded shadow policy
- [ ] #78 — Integrate prop lighting across study scenes while preserving artwork and card readability
- [ ] #79 — Qualify candle/lamp visual quality, animation and lighting performance

## Work sequence
#74 → (#75 candle and #76 lamp independently) → #77 lamp lighting → #78 scene integration → #79 qualification.

Children and parent are linked through this checklist and each child's parent reference. Native GitHub sub-issue relationships are not set because the available connector does not expose that operation.
